svg.title: Earnest Money Protection Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-emd-protection-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Earnest Money Protection Gates; subtitle: Neutral holder, verified wire, seasoned cash, live contingency; caption: The deposit is only recoverable through a live, written contingency; miss a date or waive a clause and the money is exposed.; assumptions note: Gate order follows the deposit's path from funding to closing. The 60-day seasoning rule applies to conventional, FHA, USDA and Fannie- and Freddie-backed loans.; note: Attributed to The Treasure Valley Home Show, Larry Mastropieri, Charles Nedder, Katie Anderson, Yanowitz Law Firm and Andrew Finney Team.; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the deposit going to a neutral holder such as title, a brokerage trust account or attorney escrow?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not send it; in Connecticut both attorneys must agree to release the funds.; gate: G2; question: Did the wire instructions come directly from the title company and get confirmed by your own call?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stop and call title yourself; intercepted funds are gone.; gate: G3; question: Has the cash sat in the bank account for 60 days?; pass next: G4; fail action: Treat it as non-sourceable; the closing credit can be backed out.; gate: G4; question: Is a written contingency still live, with cancellation by day 9 or 10 of a 10-day inspection period?; pass next: Deposit stays recoverable and becomes a closing credit.; fail action: Deposit is exposed; a buyer cancelling out of compliance loses it to the seller.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Is the deposit going to a neutral holder such as title, a brokerage trust account or attorney escrow?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not send it; in Connecticut both attorneys must agree to release the funds.

gate: G2; question: Did the wire instructions come directly from the title company and get confirmed by your own call?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stop and call title yourself; intercepted funds are gone.
gate: G3; question: Has the cash sat in the bank account for 60 days?; pass next: G4; fail action: Treat it as non-sourceable; the closing credit can be backed out.

gate: G4; question: Is a written contingency still live, with cancellation by day 9 or 10 of a 10-day inspection period?; pass next: Deposit stays recoverable and becomes a closing credit.; fail action: Deposit is exposed; a buyer cancelling out of compliance loses it to the seller.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order follows the deposit's path from funding to closing. The 60-day seasoning rule applies to conventional, FHA, USDA and Fannie- and Freddie-backed loans.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order follows the deposit's path from funding to closing. The 60-day seasoning rule applies to conventional, FHA,
USDA and Fannie- and Freddie-backed loans.
